Techniques to perform such model selection are subject of a well-established body of LBNL Report #2001653 research, but have not, to date, been studied in the context of radiological data fusion, except for with respect to the number of point-sources to be fit in the aPSL algorithm. Model selection issues are expected to arise (1) when one is unsure about the nature of the source (e.g., single point, multiple spatially distributed points, and amorphous, spatially distributed “lump” as in hold- up measurements) and (2) when one is unsure about the configuration of shielding environment, but one may hypothesize models based on facility designs, visual inspection, context scanner- imposed constraints, and/or operator expertise. These model selection issues will likely arise with multimodal measurements used to perform complex source reconstruction tasks with limited data. Introducing timing to the active-SDF system allows for the analysis of the source particle type and allows the algorithm to determine the distance the particle(s) have traveled from source to interaction to detector. This information becomes another spatial constraint in system equation and could prove to make SDF-coupled active interrogation methods more sensitive than the more-typical static configurations that have been subject of significant study.
